Evidence: "We chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, P Epos+k can be represented as a linear function of P Epos ." [ATT §3.5 O(n2 · d), p.6]
Evidence: "We also experimented with using learned positional embeddings [9] instead, and found that the two versions produced nearly identical results (see Table 3 row (E))." [ATT §3.5 O(n2 · d), p.6]
Evidence: "We chose the sinusoidal version because it may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than the ones encountered during training." [ATT §3.5 O(n2 · d), p.6]
The authors chose sinusoidal positional encodings because they hypothesize it would let the model learn relative positions easily, as offsets become linear functions of the encodings . [ATT §3.5 O(n2 · d), p.6]
They also found that learned embeddings gave almost the same performance, but sinusoidals may extrapolate to longer sequences . [ATT §3.5 O(n2 · d), p.6]

Evidence: "H-Net (1-stage) predominantly places boundaries at whitespace characters, closely mirroring the delimiters used by SpaceByte." [HNET §3.1 Language Modeling, p.14]
Evidence: "H-Net (1-stage) tends to draw boundaries at spacelike bytes, which is very similar to SpaceByte." [HNET §3.1 Language Modeling, p.15]
H‑Net decides chunk boundaries by learning to place them at whitespace or spacelike bytes, and in multi‑stage setups it also considers the first characters of words, using a routing module that dynamically draws boundaries based on contextual content. [HNET §3.1 Language Modeling, p.14; HNET §3.1 Language Modeling, p.15]

Evidence: "speech-to-speech generation can be drastically improved by Inner Monologue, a new method that generates text tokens as a prefix to audio tokens, while remaining compatible with streaming inference." [MOSHI §7 Conclusion, p.41]
Inner Monologue is a method that prepends text tokens before audio tokens, improving speech‑to‑speech generation while staying stream‑compatible . [MOSHI §7 Conclusion, p.41]

Evidence: "nearly 4× improvement in data efficiency over baselines" [HNET p.1]
H‑Net achieves nearly a 4× data‑efficiency gain on DNA language modeling compared to tokenized baselines . [HNET p.1]
